## Load data
```{r load-data}
df <- read_parquet("data/metrics/processed/clean-dl-training-energy-consumption-dataset.gzip") %>%
  rename(
    energy = `energy (MJ)`,
    power_draw = `average gpu power (W)`,
    training_duration = `training duration (h)`,
    used_ram = `average ram used (MB)`,
    batch_size = `batch size`,
    image_size = `image size`,
    allocated_ram = `total ram (GB)`,
    training_environment = `training environment`,
    start_time = `start time`,
  ) %>%
  filter(architecture == "inception_v3") %>%
  mutate(
    energy_per_image = (energy * 1000000) / `total seen images`, # Convert MJ to J and normalize by total seen images
    epoch_duration = training_duration / `trained epochs` * 3600, # Calculate average epoch duration in seconds
    batch_size = factor(batch_size, levels = c("32", "64", "256")),
    input_size = case_match(
      image_size,
      "(75, 75)" ~ "75x75",
      "(128, 128)" ~ "128x128",
      "(224, 224)" ~ "224x224"
    ),
    input_size = factor(input_size, levels = c("75x75", "128x128", "224x224"), ordered = TRUE),
    allocated_ram = factor(allocated_ram, levels = c("8", "16", "24", "32")),
    # Convert to a factor after renaming; case_match() returns a character vector
    dataset = case_match(
      dataset,
      "stanford_dogs" ~ "Stanford Dogs",
      "caltech101" ~ "Caltech 101"
    ),
    dataset = factor(dataset, levels = c("Caltech 101", "Stanford Dogs"))
  ) %>%
  select(energy_per_image, power_draw, epoch_duration, used_ram, batch_size, input_size, dataset, training_environment, allocated_ram, start_time)

# Set sum-to-zero contrasts in each model call so that tests do not depend on global options
factor_contrasts <- list(batch_size = "contr.sum", input_size = "contr.sum", dataset = "contr.sum")
```

df_batch_input <- df %>%
  filter(training_environment == "Desktop ML Engineer" & dataset != "ChessLive") %>%
  group_by(batch_size, input_size, dataset) %>%
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(energy_per_image, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(energy_per_image, 0.75),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    is_outlier = energy_per_image < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | energy_per_image > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)

  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is_outlier) %>%
  select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR, -is_outlier)

## Statistical analysis of the effects of batch size, input size, and dataset on energy consumption
### Linear model with dataset as a fixed effect
```{r linear-model}
model_lm <- lm(energy_per_image ~ batch_size * input_size * dataset, data = df_batch_input, contrasts = factor_contrasts)
summary(model_lm)
```

#### Check assumptions of the linear model
```{r check-dharma}
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(model_lm)
testResiduals(sim_res)
```

```{r check-model}
check_model(model_lm)
```

### Linear mixed model
```{r linear-mixed-model}
model_lmm <- lmer(
  energy_per_image ~ batch_size * input_size + (1 | dataset),
  data = df_batch_input,
  contrasts = factor_contrasts[c("batch_size", "input_size")]
)
summary(model_lmm)
```

```{r anova-mixed-model}
Anova(model_lmm, type = 3) # Type III ANOVA for mixed models
```

#### Check assumptions of the linear mixed model
```{r check-dharma-mixed}
sim_res_lmm <- simulateResiduals(model_lmm)
testResiduals(sim_res_lmm)
```

### Generalized linear model with Gamma distribution
```{r generalized-linear-model}
model_glm <- glm(
  energy_per_image ~ batch_size * input_size * dataset,
  data = df_batch_input,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  contrasts = factor_contrasts
)
summary(model_glm)
```

```{r anova-glm}
Anova(model_glm, type = 3, test.statistic = "Wald") # Type III Wald chi-square tests (sum-to-zero contrasts)
```

#### Check assumptions of the generalized linear model
```{r check-dharma-glm}
sim_res_glm <- simulateResiduals(model_glm)
testResiduals(sim_res_glm)
```

```{r check-model-glm}
check_model(model_glm)
```

### Compare models
```{r model-comparison-glm}
compare_performance(model_lm, model_lmm, model_glm, rank = TRUE)
```

### Significance testing and effect size
Type III Wald chi-square tests with sum-to-zero contrasts, consistent with the Type III tests used for the architecture and environment models. The three-way interaction is significant, so each main effect is the effect averaged equally over the levels of the other factors. We use Wald tests because Type III likelihood-ratio (and F) tests refit models without a main effect but with its interactions, and those refits do not converge here. Type II likelihood-ratio tests, which do not depend on the contrasts, are reported as a check.

The statistics are very large because the Gamma dispersion is tiny (the coefficient of variation within each configuration is below 1%), not because observations are replicated: each row is one training run.
```{r, anova-batch-input}
anova_results <- Anova(model_glm, type = 3, test.statistic = "Wald") # Type III, Wald chi-square tests
anova_results
Anova(model_glm, type = 2) # Check: Type II, likelihood-ratio chi-square tests
cat("Dispersion:", summary(model_glm)$dispersion, " residual df:", df.residual(model_glm), "\n")

non_significant_terms <- anova_results %>%
  filter(rownames(.) != "(Intercept)" & `Pr(>Chisq)` > 0.05)
```

```{r, non-significant-batch-input, eval=!(plyr::empty(non_significant_terms))}
knitr::asis_output("### Non-significant terms")
non_significant_terms
```

Because the model uses a log link, effects are multiplicative. We report them as ratios of mean energy per image (fold changes) with 95% confidence intervals.
```{r, fold-changes-batch-input}
emm_input <- emmeans(model_glm, ~ input_size | batch_size * dataset, type = "response")
input_ratios <- contrast(emm_input, method = "revpairwise", type = "response")
confint(input_ratios, adjust = "none")

emm_batch <- emmeans(model_glm, ~ batch_size | input_size * dataset, type = "response")
batch_ratios <- contrast(emm_batch, method = "revpairwise", type = "response")
confint(batch_ratios, adjust = "none")

# Marginal fold change from 75x75 to 224x224, averaged over batch sizes and datasets
confint(contrast(emmeans(model_glm, ~input_size, type = "response"), method = "revpairwise", type = "response"), adjust = "none")
```

### Post hoc tests
Estimate marginal means for the interaction between batch size and input size, conditioned on the dataset.
```{r emmeans-comparisons}
emm_lm <- emmeans(model_glm, ~ batch_size * input_size * dataset, type = "response")
emm_lm
```

#### Calculate pairwise comparisons with Tukey adjustment
```{r post-hoc-pairs}
pairwise_emm <- pairs(emm_lm, by = "dataset", adjust = "tukey")

pairwise_emm

non_significant_pairs <- as.data.frame(pairwise_emm) %>%
  filter(p.value > 0.05)
```

```{r, non-significant-pairs, eval=!(plyr::empty(non_significant_pairs))}
knitr::asis_output("### Non-significant pairwise comparisons")
non_significant_pairs
```

#### Plot the estimated marginal means.
```{r eem-plot, fig.height=8, fig.width=15}
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_lm) %>%
  filter(!is.na(response))

ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = batch_size, y = response, group = input_size, color = input_size)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~dataset) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated Marginal Means of Energy",
    x = "Batch Size",
    y = "Predicted Energy Consumption",
    color = "Input Size"
  )
```



## Statistical analysis of the effects of allocated RAM on energy consumption
Each allocated-RAM level was run in a separate session, and the 16 GB runs come from the batch- and input-size experiment on the Server. The RAM level is therefore confounded with the session (date), and the differences below may partly reflect session effects. The effect is also non-monotonic, so we compare all levels pairwise rather than describing a trend.
```{r allocated-ram-sessions}
df %>%
  filter(batch_size == "256" & input_size == "128x128" & dataset == "Stanford Dogs" & training_environment == "Server") %>%
  group_by(allocated_ram) %>%
  summarise(runs = n(), first_run = min(start_time), last_run = max(start_time))
```

### Linear model with allocated RAM as a fixed effect
```{r linear-model-allocated-ram}
model_lm_ram <- lm(energy_per_image ~ allocated_ram, data = df_allocated_ram_energy)
summary(model_lm_ram)
```
#### Check assumptions of the linear model with allocated RAM
```{r check-dharma-allocated-ram}
sim_res_ram <- simulateResiduals(model_lm_ram)
testResiduals(sim_res_ram)
```

```{r check-model-allocated-ram}
check_model(model_lm_ram)
```

#### Significance testing and effect size
```{r anova-linear-model-allocated-ram}
Anova(model_lm_ram) # One-way ANOVA (with a single factor, Types I-III coincide)
eta_squared(model_lm_ram, partial = FALSE) # Calculate eta squared for effect sizes
# Variances differ between RAM levels, so we also report Welch's ANOVA and Games-Howell comparisons
leveneTest(energy_per_image ~ allocated_ram, data = df_allocated_ram_energy)
oneway.test(energy_per_image ~ allocated_ram, data = df_allocated_ram_energy, var.equal = FALSE)
rstatix::games_howell_test(df_allocated_ram_energy, energy_per_image ~ allocated_ram)
```

#### Post hoc tests for allocated RAM
```{r post-hoc-allocated-ram}
emm_ram <- emmeans(model_lm_ram, ~allocated_ram)
emm_ram
pairs(emm_ram, adjust = "tukey")

plot(emm_ram, comparisons = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated Marginal Means of Energy by Allocated RAM",
    x = "Predicted Energy Consumption (J/image)",
    y = "Allocated RAM (GB)",
  )
```

## Statistical analysis of the effects of allocated RAM on average RAM used
### Linear model with allocated RAM as a fixed effect
```{r linear-model-average-ram-used}
model_lm_ram_used <- lm(used_ram ~ allocated_ram, data = df_allocated_ram_ram)
summary(model_lm_ram_used)
```

#### Check assumptions of the linear model with allocated RAM
```{r check-dharma-average-ram-used}
sim_res_ram_used <- simulateResiduals(model_lm_ram_used)
testResiduals(sim_res_ram_used)
```

```{r check-model-average-ram-used}
check_model(model_lm_ram_used)
```

#### Significance testing and effect size
```{r anova-linear-model-average-ram-used}
Anova(model_lm_ram_used) # One-way ANOVA (with a single factor, Types I-III coincide)
eta_squared(model_lm_ram_used, partial = FALSE) # Calculate eta squared for effect sizes
leveneTest(used_ram ~ allocated_ram, data = df_allocated_ram_ram)
oneway.test(used_ram ~ allocated_ram, data = df_allocated_ram_ram, var.equal = FALSE)
rstatix::games_howell_test(df_allocated_ram_ram, used_ram ~ allocated_ram)
```

#### Post hoc tests for allocated RAM on average RAM used
```{r post-hoc-average-ram-used}
emm_ram_used <- emmeans(model_lm_ram_used, ~allocated_ram)
emm_ram_used
pairs(emm_ram_used, adjust = "tukey")

    y = "Allocated RAM (GB)",
  )
```
